mainTopic: Stories of the מבול, the תיבה, and the miracles in אברהם's war
overview: This amud tells many stories about the מבול and the תיבה. First, the generation of נח refuses to repent, mocks his warnings, and boasts that it can stop any flood. נח answers that the water will come from right under their feet. A ברייתא and רב חסדא teach that the flood waters were thick and boiling hot, a punishment that matched their sin. The גמרא then gives four explanations of the seven days before the flood. It also explains which animals entered the תיבה, what גופר wood and the צֹהַר were, and what the three floors were for. Next come the raven's argument with נח, the ban on marital relations in the תיבה, and the dove with its olive leaf. In two conversations between שם and אליעזר, we hear how hard it was to feed every creature in the תיבה, and how אברהם beat the kings when dust and straw miraculously became weapons. The amud ends by beginning the story of נחום איש גם זו, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The generation refuses to stop sinning
steps.stepSummary: The people answer נח's warning by saying they will not change their ways.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: If so, we will not clear a path through the vineyards.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes the story from just before this section, where נח warned his generation about the coming flood. The people answer that they will keep sinning anyway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "Clearing a path through the vineyards" is a picture of leaving their bad ways behind. By saying "we will not clear it," they openly refuse to do תשובה.

keyTerms.meaning: We will clear (a path), turn aside

phrases.aramaic: אִם כֵּן, לֹא נְפַנֶּה דֶּרֶךְ כְּרָמִים.
phrases.english: If so, we will not clear a path through the vineyards.
phrases.notes: This is the end of the פסוק in איוב from just before; they mean they'll keep on sinning.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן, לֹא נְפַנֶּה דֶּרֶךְ כְּרָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the earlier story about נח's warning, which began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The generation of the מבול openly refused to repent.

steps.title: רבא: נח rebuked them with harsh words and they mocked him
steps.stepSummary: רבא reads a פסוק in איוב as describing נח rebuking his generation and their contempt for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא taught: What does the פסוק mean, "A contemptible torch in the thought of one at ease, ready for those whose foot slips"? It teaches that נח the righteous used to rebuke them. He spoke words to them that were harsh like torches, and they scorned him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא starts a new explanation of a פסוק in איוב and connects it to נח. He reads the first half of the פסוק as nod to נח's fiery rebuke and the people's scorn.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא takes the word לפיד (torch) as a picture of נח's burning, harsh words, and בוז (contempt) as the people's reaction. The second half of the פסוק, "ready for those whose foot slips," is saved for later in the story.

keyTerms.meaning: Expounded, taught a lesson from a פסוק

phrases.english: Rava expounded:
What is the meaning of that which is written:
"A contemptible torch in the thought of one who is at ease,
ready for those whose foot slips"?
phrases.notes: איוב 12:5

phrases.aramaic: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁהָיָה נֹחַ הַצַּדִּיק מוֹכִיחַ אוֹתָם,
phrases.english: It teaches that Noah the righteous would rebuke them,
and he said to them words
that were harsh like torches,
and they would treat him with contempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּרֵשׁ רָבָא: מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new teaching on a different פסוק about the same story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק in איוב describes נח's harsh rebuke and his generation's scorn.

steps.title: The people boast they can block any flood
steps.stepSummary: The people ask about the תיבה, נח warns of the מבול, and they claim to have a defense against every kind of flood.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Old man, what is this ark for? He said: The Holy One, Blessed be He, is bringing a flood on you. They said: A flood of what? If it is fire, we have a material called עליתה. If it is water from the ground, we have iron plates to cover the ground. If it is water from the sky, we have a material called עקב, and some say it is called עקש.
steps.whatsHappening: Still inside רבא's teaching, the גמרא tells the conversation between נח and the people. They list every possible flood and boast that they have a defense for each one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows the "scorn" from the פסוק in action: they treat God's warning like an engineering problem they can solve. Their plan to plate over the ground sets up נח's answer in the next step: the water will come up from right under their own feet.

keyTerms.meaning: A material they claimed could protect against fire

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: זָקֵן, תֵּיבָה זוֹ לָמָּה?
phrases.english: They said to him: Old man, why this ark?
He said to them: The Holy One, Blessed be He,
is bringing the flood upon you.
They said: A flood of what?
If it is a flood of fire,

phrases.aramaic: יֵשׁ לָנוּ דָּבָר אֶחָד וַעֲלִיתָה שְׁמָהּ.
phrases.english: we have one thing, and its name is alita.
phrases.notes: They are bragging that this material would protect them from fire.

phrases.english: And if He brings one of water,
if He brings it from the earth,
we have plates of iron
with which we can cover the ground.
And if He brings it from the heavens,
we have a thing and its name is ekev,
phrases.notes: They mean something that would soak up the rain.

phrases.english: and some say: its name is ikkesh.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: זָקֵן, תֵּיבָה זוֹ לָמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the scorn described in step 2 through the actual conversation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The generation mocked נח by claiming they could stop any flood.

steps.title: נח: The water will come from between your feet
steps.stepSummary: נח answers that God will bring the water up from right under them, and this explains the end of the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: He will bring it from between the heels of your feet, as it says, "ready for those whose foot slips."
steps.whatsHappening: נח answers their boasting, and this finishes רבא's explanation of the פסוק. The water will come from a place none of their defenses can cover.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their last defense was called עקב, and נח answers with עקבי רגליכם, "your heels," turning their own word against them. This explains the end of the פסוק, "ready for those whose foot slips": the flood was prepared to come right from under their feet.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is said (introduces a פסוק)

steps.whatToRemember: רבא reads the whole פסוק in איוב as the story of נח: harsh rebuke (לפיד), the people's scorn (בוז), and a flood from under their feet (מועדי רגל).

phrases.english: He said to them: He will bring it
from between the heels of your feet,
as it is said: "Ready for those whose foot slips."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶם: הוּא מֵבִיא מִבֵּין עִקְּבֵי רַגְלֵיכֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the boasts in step 3 and finishes reading the פסוק from step 2.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: No human defense can stop God's punishment. The flood could come from right beneath them.

steps.title: ברייתא: The flood waters were thick like semen
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads the same פסוק to teach that the flood waters were thick.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: The waters of the flood were as thick as semen, as it says, "ready for those whose foot slips."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that uses the same end of the פסוק to describe what the flood water was like.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the word רגל (foot) is read as a polite way of referring to the body part used in relations. So the waters were thick like semen, matching the sexual sins of that generation.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read רגל here as a literal foot. In this ברייתא it is a polite word for the body part, which is why it connects to semen.

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita:
The waters of the flood were thick like semen,
as it is said: "Ready for those whose foot slips."
phrases.notes: Here "foot" is a polite way of naming the body part, not a real foot.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא: מֵימֵי הַמַּבּוּל קָשִׁים כְּשִׁכְבַת זֶרַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second reading of the same words of the פסוק used in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The flood waters were thick like semen, matching the generation's sin.

steps.title: רב חסדא: Sinned with hot, punished with hot
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא teaches that the punishment matched the sin: they sinned with hot fluid and were punished with boiling water.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: With hot fluid they corrupted themselves in sin, and with hot water they were punished.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא adds another way the punishment matched the sin. The flood waters were boiling hot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is מדה כנגד מדה (measure for measure). Their sin involved hot semen, so their punishment was hot water. The proof comes in the next step.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a common idea in חז"ל: God's punishment often fits the sin exactly, מדה כנגד מדה.

phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda said:
With hot [fluid] they corrupted themselves in sin,
and with hot [water] they were punished.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: בְּרוֹתְחִין קִלְקְלוּ בַּעֲבֵירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the ברייתא's link between the flood and their sin, adding that the water was hot.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The flood waters were boiling hot, as a measure-for-measure punishment.

steps.title: Proof: "calmed" means cooled from heat
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא's source compares the word שכך in the flood story to the same word in מגילת אסתר, where it describes anger cooling down.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is written here: "And the waters calmed," and it is written there: "And the king's anger calmed."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for רב חסדא's claim that the water was hot. It matches one word in two different פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In אסתר, שככה describes the king's hot anger cooling down. So when the תורה uses the same word for the flood waters, it means the waters were hot and then cooled.

phrases.english: It is written here: "And the waters calmed,"
phrases.notes: בראשית 8:1

phrases.english: and it is written there: "And the king's anger calmed."
phrases.notes: אסתר 7:10. The same word, so it means the heat went down in both places.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּתִיב הָכָא: ״וַיָּשֹׁכּוּ הַמָּיִם״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for רב חסדא's statement in step 6.
steps.raayaObject: רב חסדא's claim that the flood waters were hot.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A word link between "וישכו המים" (בראשית 8:1) and "וחמת המלך שככה" (אסתר 7:10).

steps.title: What were the seven days before the flood?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a פסוק about seven days before the flood and asks what those days were for.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And it was after the seven days, and the waters of the flood were upon the earth." What was the nature of those seven days?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic. It quotes a פסוק and asks what the seven-day delay was for, setting up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the flood came only after seven days, which seems like an unexplained wait. The גמרא asks what was special about those days. Steps 9 through 12 give four different answers.

phrases.english: "And it was after the seven days,
and the waters of the flood were upon the earth":
phrases.notes: בראשית 7:10

phrases.english: What is the nature of the seven days?

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה טִיבָם שֶׁל שִׁבְעַת הַיָּמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new פסוק and a new question about the flood story.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the פסוק mentions a seven-day period before the flood began, and what happened during it.

steps.title: The seven days were mourning for מתושלח
steps.stepSummary: רב answers that the seven days were days of mourning for מתושלח, which teaches that eulogizing צדיקים holds back punishment.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: These were the days of mourning for מתושלח. This teaches you that eulogies for the righteous hold back a punishment from coming.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its first answer to the question from step 8. רב says the seven days were mourning days for the צדיק מתושלח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The world was already supposed to be punished, but the flood waited seven days. רב learns from this that mourning and eulogizing a צדיק can delay a punishment.

keyTerms.meaning: מתושלח, the righteous grandfather of נח
A eulogy, mourning speech for someone who died

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a lasting lesson: honoring a צדיק after he dies can protect the world.

phrases.english: Rav said:
These were the days of mourning for Methuselah,
phrases.notes: 'These' means the seven days before the flood from the פסוק in step 8 (בראשית 7:10).

phrases.english: to teach you that the eulogies of the righteous
hold back the punishment from coming.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: אֵלּוּ יְמֵי אֲבֵילוּת שֶׁל מְתוּשֶׁלַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The seven days were mourning for מתושלח; eulogizing צדיקים delays punishment.

steps.title: The seven days of the world running backward
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: for seven days הקב"ה changed the order of creation, and the sun rose in the west and set in the east.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: these were seven days in which הקב"ה changed the order of creation for them, so the sun rose in the west and set in the east.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, different answer about the seven days. During them, nature was turned around.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer does not say the days were a delay for mourning. It says they were days of a strange sign: the sun moved backward, which should have shaken the people.

keyTerms.meaning: The order of creation, the normal way nature works

phrases.english: Another explanation: "After the seven [days]" —
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is added in the corrected wording.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁשִּׁינָּה עֲלֵיהֶם הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא סֵדֶר בְּרֵאשִׁית,
phrases.english: in which the Holy One, Blessed be He, changed the order of creation for them,
so that the sun would rise in the west
and set in the east.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר אַחֵר: לְשִׁבְעַת הַיָּמִים שֶׁשִּׁינָּה עֲלֵיהֶם הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא סֵדֶר בְּרֵאשִׁית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the same question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: During the seven days nature was reversed: the sun rose in the west.

steps.title: A long time, then a short time
steps.stepSummary: A third answer: הקב"ה first gave them a long period, and afterward a short period of seven days.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: הקב"ה set a long period of time for them, and after that a short period.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a third answer. The seven days were a final short period that came after a long one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the seven days are an extra short period after the long one had already ended. The point is that הקב"ה kept giving the people more time.

phrases.aramaic: דָּבָר אַחֵר: שֶׁקָּבַע לָהֶם הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
phrases.english: Another explanation: that the Holy One, Blessed be He, set for them

phrases.aramaic: זְמַן גָּדוֹל, וְאַחַר כָּךְ זְמַן קָטָן.
phrases.english: a long period, and afterward a short period.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר אַחֵר: שֶׁקָּבַע לָהֶם הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא זְמַן גָּדוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third answer to the same question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The seven days were a short final period after a long one.

steps.title: A taste of עולם הבא
steps.stepSummary: A fourth answer: during the seven days הקב"ה gave them a taste of עולם הבא, so they would know what good they had lost.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: these were seven days in which He gave them a taste of עולם הבא, so that they would know what good they kept from themselves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its fourth and last answer about the seven days. They were days of tasting עולם הבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer shows the people what they were losing because of their sins. Before the punishment, they got a small taste of the reward they could have had.

keyTerms.meaning: Something like עולם הבא, a sample of it

steps.whatToRemember: The seven days before the מבול get four answers: mourning for מתושלח, nature reversed, a short final period, and a taste of עולם הבא.

phrases.english: Another explanation: "After the seven days" —
in which He gave them a taste of the World-to-Come,

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֵי שֶׁיֵּדְעוּ מָה טוֹבָה מָנְעוּ מֵהֶן.
phrases.english: so that they would know what good they kept from themselves.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר אַחֵר: לְשִׁבְעַת הַיָּמִים שֶׁהִטְעִימָם מֵעֵין הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The fourth and last answer to the same question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The seven days gave them a taste of עולם הבא.

steps.title: Can animals be husband and wife?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the פסוק telling נח to take clean animals 'man and wife', and asks: do animals have marriage?
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'Of every clean animal you shall take for yourself seven and seven, a man and his wife.' Do animals have marriage?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It points out a strange word in the פסוק: animals are called 'man and his wife'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Animals don't get married, so why does the תורה use marriage words for them? The גמרא wants to know what this wording is teaching.

phrases.english: "Of every clean animal you shall take for yourself
phrases.notes: בראשית 7:2

phrases.english: seven and seven, a man and his wife."
Does an animal have marriage?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִישׁוּת לִבְהֵמָה מִי אִית לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic in the flood story
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What do the words 'man and his wife' mean when said about animals?

steps.title: Only animals that stayed with their own kind
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר נחמני in the name of רבי יונתן explains: נח took only animals that had not been involved in the sin of mixing with other kinds.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נחמני said in the name of רבי יונתן: It means from those animals with which no sin was done.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. 'Man and his wife' means animals that stayed faithful to their own kind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The marriage words are not about a wedding. They tell us that נח took only animals not involved in the sin of mating with other species.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani said that Rabbi Yonatan said:
From those with which a sin was not done.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Man and his wife' means animals not involved in the sin of mixing with other kinds.

steps.title: How did נח know?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how נח could know which animals were not involved in the sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: How did he know?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question on the answer it just gave. How could נח tell which animals had sinned?
steps.deeperAnalysis: You can't see an animal's past by looking at it. So the answer from step 14 raises a practical question.

phrases.english: From where did he know?

steps.triggerLanguage: מְנָא יְדַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follow-up question on step 14
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How did נח identify the animals that had not sinned?

steps.title: The ark let in only the right animals
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says נח passed the animals in front of the תיבה: any animal the תיבה took in had not sinned, and any it did not take in had sinned.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: He passed them in front of the ark. Any animal the ark took in was known not to have sinned. Any animal the ark did not take in was known to have sinned.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the question. The תיבה itself chose the animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נח did not have to figure it out himself. The תיבה worked like a test: it took in the right animals and kept out the others.

phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda said:
He passed them in front of the ark,
any animal that the ark took in —
it was known that a sin had not been done with them,
and any animal that the ark did not take in —
it was known that a sin had been done with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: שֶׁהֶעֱבִירָן לִפְנֵי הַתֵּיבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The תיבה accepted only the animals that had not sinned.

steps.title: Only animals that came by themselves
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו gives a different answer: נח took only the animals that came to the תיבה on their own.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: From those that came on their own.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו gives a second answer to how נח knew. The right animals came by themselves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of a test at the door, רבי אבהו says the animals showed up on their own. Coming by themselves showed they were the ones meant to be saved.
steps.whatToRemember: נח took only animals that had not sinned. רב חסדא says the תיבה picked them, and רבי אבהו says they came on their own.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר: מֵאוֹתָן הַבָּאִין מֵאֵילֵיהֶן.
phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said: From those that came on their own.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר: מֵאוֹתָן הַבָּאִין מֵאֵילֵיהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to step 15, different from רב חסדא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: נח took the animals that came to him on their own.

steps.title: What is גופר wood?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the command to build the תיבה from עצי גופר and asks what גופר is.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'Make yourself an ark of gopher wood.' What is gopher?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new question about the flood story. It asks what kind of wood גופר is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word גופר is unclear, and the תורה doesn't explain it. The גמרא wants to know which tree it is.

keyTerms.meaning: Gopher wood, the wood of the תיבה

phrases.english: "Make yourself an ark of gopher wood."
phrases.notes: בראשית 6:14

phrases.english: What is gopher?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי גּוֹפֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic

steps.title: גופר is מבליגה, or some say גולמיש
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא reports that the school of רבי שילא said גופר is מבליגה, and some say it is גולמיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא said: In the school of רבי שילא they say it is מבליגה. And some say: גולמיש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers what גופר is. Two names of trees are given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer simply names the tree. There are two versions of what the school of רבי שילא said: מבליגה or גולמיש.

keyTerms.meaning: The study hall of רבי שילא
And some say it this way
The name of a kind of tree
The name of a kind of tree, a willow

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא: אָמְרִי דְּבֵי רַבִּי שֵׁילָא,
phrases.english: Rav Adda said: They say in the school of Rabbi Sheila,
this is mavliga.
phrases.notes: מבליגה and גולמיש are both names of kinds of trees.

phrases.english: And some say: gulamish.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא: אָמְרִי דְּבֵי רַבִּי שֵׁילָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: גופר is מבליגה, or according to another version, גולמיש.

steps.title: The צֹהַר: precious stones that gave light
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that the צֹהַר of the תיבה was precious stones and pearls that gave light like midday.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the פסוק 'Make a צֹהַר for the תיבה,' רבי יוחנן said: The Holy One told נח, 'Set precious stones and pearls in it, so they shine for you like the midday sun.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next פסוק about building the תיבה and explains the word צֹהַר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of a window, רבי יוחנן reads צֹהַר as a light source. He links it to צׇהֳרַיִם, the bright noon sun, so the gems lit the inside of the תיבה.

keyTerms.meaning: A light source for the תיבה, explained here as glowing gems
Midday, when the sun is brightest

phrases.english: "A tzohar you shall make for the ark"
phrases.notes: בראשית 6:16

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְנֹחַ,
phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Noah:
Set precious stones and pearls in it,
so that they will shine for you like midday.
phrases.notes: צֹהַר and צׇהֳרַיִם sound alike, and that is how רבי יוחנן gets his reading.

steps.triggerLanguage: צֹהַר תַּעֲשֶׂה לַתֵּבָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the word גופר to the next word in the building instructions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The צֹהַר was precious stones and pearls that lit the תיבה like the noon sun.

steps.title: Narrowing the top keeps the ark standing
steps.stepSummary: The תיבה narrowed to one אמה at the top because that shape let it stand steady.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And finish it to an אמה at the top,' because that is how it stays standing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the תיבה was built narrowing to just one אמה at the top.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A shape that is wide below and narrow above is stable and does not tip over. So the פסוק's design is about keeping the תיבה upright.

keyTerms.meaning: A cubit, a measure of about an arm's length

phrases.english: "And to a cubit you shall finish it above"
phrases.notes: בראשית 6:16

phrases.english: because in this way it stands.
phrases.notes: Wide at the bottom and narrow at the top means it won't tip over. The word in square brackets is added in the corrected wording.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶל אַמָּה תְּכַלֶּנָּה מִלְמַעְלָה דִּבְהָכִי הוּא דְּקָיְימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues with the next phrase of the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Narrowing the top to an אמה kept the תיבה stable.

steps.title: What each of the three floors was for
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the bottom floor was for dung, the middle for animals, and the top for people.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Make it with lower, second, and third floors.' A ברייתא taught: the bottom floor was for dung, the middle for animals, and the top for people.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that explains why the תיבה needed three floors.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק only says to build three levels. The ברייתא tells us what each level held, so the waste stayed apart from the animals and the people.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: "With lower, second and third stories shall you make it"
phrases.notes: בראשית 6:16

phrases.english: It was taught: the bottom ones for dung,
the middle ones for the animals,
the top ones for people.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּחְתִּיִּם שְׁנִיִּם וּשְׁלִשִׁים תַּעֲשֶׂהָ תָּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes explaining the building פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bottom floor for dung, middle for animals, top for people.

steps.title: The raven's winning argument against נח
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says the raven gave נח an unbeatable answer: 'Your Master hates me, and you hate me.'
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And he sent out the raven.' ריש לקיש said: The raven gave נח a winning answer. It said to him: 'Your Master hates me, and you hate me too.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא jumps to the end of the flood, when נח sent out the raven. ריש לקיש introduces the raven's complaint. The next steps explain it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the raven went 'back and forth' instead of flying off. ריש לקיש fills in that it argued with נח. First he gives its main claim; the support comes next.

phrases.english: "And he sent forth the raven"
phrases.notes: בראשית 8:7

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
The raven gave Noah a winning answer.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: רַבְּךָ שׂוֹנְאֵנִי וְאַתָּה שְׂנֵאתָנִי.
phrases.english: It said to him: Your Master hates me, and you hate me.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַיְשַׁלַּח אֶת הָעֹרֵב אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ תְּשׁוּבָה נִיצַּחַת הֱשִׁיבוֹ עוֹרֵב לְנֹחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic: from building the תיבה to the end of the flood.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The raven claimed both הקב״ה and נח hated it.

steps.title: Why the raven says it is hated
steps.stepSummary: The raven proves its claim: הקב״ה saved only two of each impure kind, and נח sent an impure bird instead of a pure one.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Your Master hates me': He said to take seven of each pure kind but only two of each impure kind. 'And you hate me': you leave the kinds that have seven and send one from a kind that has only two.
steps.whatsHappening: The raven backs up each half of its complaint with a reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Against הקב״ה: the raven is impure, so only one pair was saved. Against נח: there were plenty of pure birds, yet he risked one of the only two ravens.

phrases.english: Your Master hates me:

phrases.aramaic: מִן הַטְּהוֹרִין שִׁבְעָה, מִן הַטְּמֵאִים שְׁנַיִם,
phrases.english: from the pure ones seven, from the impure ones two,
phrases.notes: He is pointing to the command in בראשית 7:2-3 about how many of each kind to bring.

phrases.english: and you hate me:
for you leave aside the kind with seven
and send from the kind with two.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבְּךָ שׂוֹנְאֵנִי מִן הַטְּהוֹרִין שִׁבְעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains and supports the claim made in step 23.
steps.raayaObject: The raven's claim that הקב״ה and נח both hate it.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Only two impure animals were saved, versus seven pure, and נח chose an impure bird to send.

steps.title: The raven's challenge: the world could lose my kind
steps.stepSummary: The raven asks: if heat or cold kills me, won't a whole kind be missing from the world? Or maybe you want my wife?
steps.simpleTranslation: 'If the angel of heat or the angel of cold strikes me, won't the world be missing a whole kind of creature? Or maybe you need my wife?'
steps.whatsHappening: The raven ends its argument with two sharp questions that challenge נח's choice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since there is only one pair of ravens, if this raven dies the species dies out. The raven also accuses נח of sending it away to be with its mate.

keyTerms.meaning: The angel in charge of heat
The angel in charge of cold
A creature, a kind of being

steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש's raven argues that sending it was unfair and dangerous, since its whole kind depended on just one pair.

phrases.aramaic: אִם פּוֹגֵעַ בִּי שַׂר חַמָּה אוֹ שַׂר צִנָּה,
phrases.english: If the angel of heat or the angel of cold strikes me,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נִמְצָא עוֹלָם חָסֵר בְּרִיָּה אַחַת?
phrases.english: will the world not be found missing one kind of creature?
Or perhaps it is my wife you need?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם פּוֹגֵעַ בִּי שַׂר חַמָּה אוֹ שַׂר צִנָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the danger to the raven's species and a final accusation.
steps.kashyaTarget: נח's decision to send the raven out of the תיבה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: With only one pair of ravens, risking one endangers the whole species; also נח may have had a bad motive.

steps.title: נח answers the raven with a קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: נח calls the raven wicked and argues: if my own wife is forbidden to me now, surely your mate is.
steps.simpleTranslation: נח said to the raven: Wicked one! If the one who is normally permitted to me, my wife, is forbidden to me now, then the one who is always forbidden to me, your mate, is surely forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: נח answers the raven's accusation that maybe he wants the raven's wife. He uses a קל וחומר to show how silly the claim is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The raven suggested נח had a bad motive for sending it away. נח points out that in the תיבה even his own wife is off-limits to him. If what is normally allowed is now forbidden, then what is always forbidden is certainly forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: All the more so (a קל וחומר)

phrases.english: He said to him: Wicked one!
phrases.notes: נח is talking to the raven here.

phrases.english: With the one permitted to me, I was forbidden
phrases.notes: He means his own wife.

phrases.english: with the one forbidden to me, all the more so!
phrases.notes: He means the raven's mate, which a person may never be with anyway.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: רָשָׁע! בַּמּוּתָּר לִי נֶאֱסַר לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the raven's challenge from step 25
steps.terutzResolutionType: קל וחומר that rejects the raven's suggested motive
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The raven suggested נח might want its mate.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even נח's own wife was forbidden in the תיבה, so the raven's mate is certainly forbidden.

steps.title: How do we know relations were forbidden in the ark?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that relations were forbidden in the תיבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know that they were forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: נח's answer assumed that relations were forbidden in the תיבה. The גמרא now asks for the source, setting up the proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קל וחומר depends on the claim that נח's wife was forbidden to him. The פסוק never says this directly, so the גמרא wants to know where it comes from.

phrases.english: And from where do we know that they were forbidden?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמְנָלַן דְּנֶאֶסְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the assumption in step 26
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source that marital relations were forbidden in the תיבה

steps.title: The order of the family in the verses shows the ban
steps.stepSummary: Going into the תיבה, the men and women are listed separately. Coming out, each husband is listed with his wife. רבי יוחנן learns from this that relations were forbidden inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And you shall come into the ark, you, and your sons, and your wife, and your sons' wives with you.' And it is written: 'Go out of the ark, you and your wife, and your sons and your sons' wives with you.' And רבי יוחנן said: From here we learn that they were forbidden in marital relations.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by comparing two פסוקים. One describes entering the תיבה and one describes leaving it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When they enter, the men are grouped together ('you and your sons') and the women are grouped together. When they leave, each man is paired with his wife ('you and your wife'). רבי יוחנן reads this change as showing that husbands and wives were kept apart inside the תיבה.
steps.confusionAlert: Look closely at the order of the words. The same people are in both פסוקים; only the pairing changes.

phrases.english: As it is written:
"And you shall come into the ark,
you, and your sons, and your wife,
and your sons' wives with you"
phrases.notes: בראשית 6:18

phrases.english: And it is written: "Go out of the ark,
you and your wife,
and your sons and your sons' wives with you."
phrases.notes: בראשית 8:16

phrases.english: And רבי יוחנן said:
From here (they said) that they were forbidden
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets. The meaning stays the same.

phrases.english: in marital relations.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: ״וּבָאתָ אֶל הַתֵּבָה אַתָּה וּבָנֶיךָ וְאִשְׁתְּךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 27
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The change in how the family is grouped, between entering and leaving the תיבה, shows that relations were forbidden inside.

steps.title: Three broke the ban and were punished
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the dog, the raven, and חם had relations in the תיבה, and each was punished.
steps.simpleTranslation: תנו רבנן: Three had relations in the ark, and all of them were punished: the dog, the raven, and חם. The dog gets tied, the raven spits, and חם was struck in his skin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about three who ignored the ban in the תיבה. It lists the punishment each one received.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This builds on the ban just proven in step 28. The ברייתא names the three who broke it and says each one's punishment stayed with it: the dog is tied, the raven spits, and חם's skin was struck.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Three had relations in the ark,
and all of them were punished.
The dog, the raven, and חם.
The dog gets tied,
the raven spits,
חם was struck in his skin.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שְׁלֹשָׁה שִׁמְּשׁוּ בַּתֵּיבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of the ban proven in step 28
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dog, the raven, and חם had relations in the תיבה, and each was punished.

steps.title: The pure birds lived near the righteous
steps.stepSummary: From the words 'from him' in the פסוק about the dove, רבי ירמיה learns that the pure birds lived near the צדיקים in the תיבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And he sent the dove from him, to see if the waters had lessened.' רבי ירמיה said: From here we learn that the dwelling of pure birds is with the righteous.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next פסוק, about נח sending the dove. רבי ירמיה draws a lesson from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the dove was sent 'from him', meaning from right where נח was. That shows the dove, a pure bird, was living near נח. רבי ירמיה learns that pure birds live with the צדיקים.
steps.whatToRemember: In the ark the raven was sent away while the pure dove lived right beside נח. The צדיקים and the pure birds stayed together.

phrases.english: "And he sent the dove from him
phrases.notes: בראשית 8:8

phrases.english: to see if the waters had lessened."
רבי ירמיה said:
From here we learn that the dwelling
of pure birds is with the righteous.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״וַיְשַׁלַּח אֶת הַיּוֹנָה מֵאִתּוֹ לִרְאוֹת הֲקַלּוּ הַמַּיִם״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next פסוק in the story of the flood
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The word 'from him' shows that the pure birds lived near the צדיקים in the תיבה.

steps.title: The dove's prayer: bitter food from God rather than sweet food from people
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains that the bitter olive leaf in the יונה's mouth was a message: she would rather have bitter food from ה' than sweet food from people.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And behold, a plucked olive leaf in her mouth.' רבי אלעזר says: The יונה said to ה', 'Master of the world, let my food be bitter like an olive but come from Your hand, and not sweet like honey but come from the hand of people.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new פסוק about the יונה, and רבי אלעזר explains why she brought back a bitter olive leaf.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The olive leaf is bitter. רבי אלעזר reads it as the יונה's choice: depending on ה', even for bitter food, is better than depending on people for sweet food. The word טָרָף is understood as 'food,' and the next step asks how we know that.

keyTerms.meaning: flesh and blood, meaning a human being

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a well-known lesson about trusting ה' for one's livelihood instead of relying on people.

phrases.english: "And behold, a plucked olive leaf was in her mouth."
phrases.notes: בראשית 8:11

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar says:

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרָה יוֹנָה לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא,
phrases.english: The dove said before the Holy One, Blessed be He:
Master of the world,
let my food be bitter like an olive
and placed in Your hand,
and let it not be sweet like honey
and placed in the hand of flesh and blood.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהִנֵּה עֲלֵה זַיִת טָרָף בְּפִיהָ אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of explanations of the פסוקים about the יונה and the תיבה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The olive leaf shows that the יונה preferred bitter food from ה' over sweet food from people.

steps.title: How do we know the word טרף means food?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a source that the word טרף refers to food.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know that this word 'טרף' is a word for food?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to check a building block of רבי אלעזר's explanation: does טרף really mean food?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק, טרף could simply mean 'plucked.' רבי אלעזר's whole lesson depends on reading it as 'food.' So the גמרא wants a source for that meaning.

keyTerms.meaning: a word, a way of speaking

phrases.english: From where is it understood
that this word "טרף" is a word for food?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי מַשְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the word meaning that step 31 relies on.

steps.title: Proof from משלי: הטריפני means feed me
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the פסוק 'הטריפני לחם חקי' from משלי, where the same root clearly means feeding.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'Feed me my allotted bread.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק where the same root טרף plainly means 'to feed.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: In משלי, 'הַטְרִיפֵנִי לֶחֶם חֻקִּי' can only mean 'give me my bread to eat.' Since the root clearly means food there, it can mean food in the יונה's פסוק too. That supports רבי אלעזר's reading.

keyTerms.meaning: my allotted bread, my set portion

phrases.english: As it is written:
"Feed me my allotted bread."
phrases.notes: משלי 30:8

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב הַטְרִיפֵנִי לֶחֶם חֻקִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 32.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: In משלי the same root clearly means feeding, so טרף can mean food.

steps.title: Their families came out, not necessarily the same animals
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן reads 'למשפחותיהם יצאו' to mean that their families came out of the תיבה, not necessarily the same animals that went in.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'By their families they went out of the ark.' רבי יוחנן says: 'Their families' came out, and not 'they' themselves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new פסוק about leaving the תיבה, and רבי יוחנן makes a short reading of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק does not say 'they went out.' It says 'their families went out.' רבי יוחנן learns from this that some of the animals that went in did not come out themselves, and their offspring came out instead.

keyTerms.meaning: they went out of the ark

phrases.english: "By their families they went out of the ark,"
phrases.notes: בראשית 8:19

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan says:
"Their families," and not "they."
phrases.notes: He means their families, the young born in the תיבה, came out, and not necessarily the very same animals that went in.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתֵיהֶם יָצְאוּ מִן הַתֵּבָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new פסוק and a new teaching about leaving the תיבה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The animals' families came out, not necessarily the same animals that went in.

steps.title: אליעזר asks שם what his family did in the ark
steps.stepSummary: רב חנא בר ביזנא reports that אליעזר quoted the same פסוק to שם and asked him where his family was and what they did.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנא בר ביזנא says: אליעזר said to שם the Great: It is written, 'By their families they went out of the ark.' Where were you?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a story. אליעזר asks שם, who was actually in the תיבה, what life was like there for him and his family.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same פסוק about the animals' families is used here as the opening of the conversation. אליעזר wants to know what the people were doing while all the animals were inside. This question sets up שם's long answer in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: שם the Great, son of נח

phrases.english: Rav Chana bar Bizna says:
Eliezer said to Shem the Great:
phrases.notes: This is אליעזר, אברהם's servant, speaking with נח's son שם.

phrases.english: It is written: "By their families they went out of the ark."
Where were you (all)?
phrases.notes: He means: what were you and your family doing to take care of all those animals?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לֵיהּ אֱלִיעֶזֶר לְשֵׁם רַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same פסוק from step 34 to open a story.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What שם's family did while caring for the animals in the תיבה.

steps.title: שם answers: we suffered greatly feeding each creature on its schedule
steps.stepSummary: שם answers that they had great suffering in the תיבה, because they fed every creature at its own time, day or night.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: We had great suffering in the ark. A creature that is usually fed by day, we fed by day. One that is usually fed at night, we fed at night.
steps.whatsHappening: שם begins his answer: life in the תיבה was very hard work, because each animal had to be fed on its own schedule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The family could not feed everyone at one time. They followed each creature's natural schedule, so they worked day and night. The next steps give specific examples.

phrases.english: They said to him:
We had great suffering in the ark.
A creature that is usually fed by day —
we fed it by day;
one that is usually fed at night —
we fed it at night.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ צַעַר גָּדוֹל הָיָה לָנוּ בַּתֵּיבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אליעזר's question from step 35.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They worked very hard, feeding each creature at its own natural time.

steps.title: The chameleon: how נח found out what it eats
steps.stepSummary: נח did not know what the chameleon ate until a worm fell from a pomegranate and it ate the worm. After that he prepared wormy bran for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: This chameleon: Father did not know what it ate. One day he was sitting and peeling a pomegranate. A worm fell out, and the chameleon ate it. From then on he would knead bran for it, and when the bran became wormy, the chameleon would eat it.
steps.whatsHappening: שם gives his first example of how hard it was: they did not even know what some animals ate.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נח had no idea how to feed the chameleon. He found out by chance, when it ate a worm. From then on he made food that would grow worms, so it would have the right food.

phrases.english: This chameleon —

phrases.aramaic: לָא הֲוָה יָדַע אַבָּא מָה אָכְלָה.
phrases.english: Father did not know what it eats.
One day he was sitting
and peeling a pomegranate;
a worm fell out of it, and it ate it.
phrases.notes: The one eating is the chameleon.

phrases.english: From then on
he would knead bran for it,
and when it got wormy, it would eat it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי זְקִיתָא לָא הֲוָה יָדַע אַבָּא מָה אָכְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: First example inside שם's answer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even finding out what each animal ate took effort; נח learned the chameleon's food by chance.

steps.title: The lion was kept alive by a fever, with support from רב
steps.stepSummary: The lion did not need to be fed because a fever sustained it. רב's teaching that a fever can sustain someone for six to twelve days supports this.
steps.simpleTranslation: The lion: a fever fed it. As רב said: no less than six days and no more than twelve days, a fever feeds a person.
steps.whatsHappening: שם gives a second example: the lion did not need food, because it had a fever. The גמרא then brings רב's teaching to show that a fever can really keep someone alive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of feeding the lion, the fever kept it going. רב's statement backs this up: someone with a fever can go between six and twelve days without needing to eat.

phrases.english: The lion — a fever fed it,
as Rav said:
Not less than six
and not more than twelve
does a fever feed.
phrases.notes: He means days: a fever can sustain someone for six to twelve days.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַרְיָא אֶישָּׁתָא זַנְתֵּיהּ דְּאָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second example inside שם's answer, supported by רב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The lion was sustained by a fever, and רב teaches that a fever sustains for six to twelve days.

steps.title: The phoenix did not ask for food and was blessed never to die
steps.stepSummary: נח found the phoenix lying quietly. It said it did not want to bother him because he was busy, so נח blessed it never to die, and a פסוק in איוב is brought about it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The phoenix: Father found it lying in a corner of the ark. He said to it: Don't you want food? It said to him: I saw that you were busy, so I said I would not trouble you. He said to it: May it be God's will that you never die. As it says: 'And I said, I will die with my nest, and like the חול I will have many days.'
steps.whatsHappening: שם gives his last example: the phoenix was so considerate that it did not ask for food, and נח blessed it with endless life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the other animals, the phoenix held back from asking for food so it would not add to נח's burden. As a reward, נח blessed it never to die. The פסוק in איוב, which speaks of living many days like the חול, is read as referring to this bird.
steps.whatToRemember: שם describes the תיבה as a year of nonstop care: feeding each creature at its own time and learning what each one needed. The phoenix, which did not want to bother נח, was blessed never to die.

phrases.english: The phoenix —
Father found it
lying in a corner of the ark.
He said to it: Don't you want food?
It said to him:
I saw that you were busy,
so I said, I will not trouble you.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: יְהֵא רַעֲוָא דְּלָא תְּמוּת,
phrases.english: He said to it: May it be (God's) will that you not die,
as it says:

phrases.aramaic: ״וָאֹמַר עִם קִנִּי אֶגְוָע וְכַחוֹל אַרְבֶּה יָמִים״.
phrases.english: "And I said, I will die with my nest, and like the חול I will have many days."
phrases.notes: איוב 29:18. The גמרא reads 'חול' here as the name of this long-living bird.

steps.triggerLanguage: אוּרְשִׁינָה אַשְׁכְּחֵיהּ אַבָּא דְּגָנֵי בְּסַפְנָא דְּתֵיבוֹתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final example inside שם's answer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The phoenix did not trouble נח for food, so נח blessed it never to die, as the פסוק in איוב hints.

steps.title: שם asks אליעזר how they fought the kings
steps.stepSummary: רב חנה בר לואי reports that שם רבא asked אליעזר what they did when the kings of the east and west attacked them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנה בר לואי said: שם the Great asked אליעזר, 'When the kings of the east and the west came against you, what did you do?'
steps.whatsHappening: Another conversation between שם and אליעזר begins. שם asks a question, and this step sets up אליעזר's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, אליעזר asked שם about the תיבה. Now the roles switch, and שם asks אליעזר about the war of the kings in אברהם's time. The question is simple: how could a small group beat powerful kings?

keyTerms.meaning: שם the Great, the son of נח
kings of the east and the west

phrases.english: Rav Chana bar Levai said:
Shem the Great said to Eliezer:
phrases.notes: This is אליעזר, the servant of אברהם.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אֲתוֹ עֲלַיְיכוּ מַלְכֵי מִזְרָח וּמַעֲרָב,
phrases.english: When the kings of the east and the west came upon you,
phrases.notes: He means the four kings who went to war in אברהם's time.

phrases.english: what did you do?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתּוּן הֵיכִי עֲבְידִיתוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of שם and אליעזר conversations, now with שם asking.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How אברהם's household fought and beat the kings of east and west.

steps.title: אליעזר answers that dust and straw became weapons
steps.stepSummary: אליעזר answers that הקדוש ברוך הוא seated אברהם at His right, and the dust they threw became swords and the straw became arrows.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: הקדוש ברוך הוא brought אברהם and sat him at His right. We would throw dust and it turned into swords, and straw and it turned into arrows.
steps.whatsHappening: אליעזר answers שם's question. They won by a miracle, not by real weapons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer explains how a few people beat mighty kings: ה׳ was on אברהם's side. Plain dust and straw became swords and arrows, so the victory came completely from ה׳.

keyTerms.meaning: He sat him at His right

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אַיְיתִי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְאַבְרָהָם
phrases.english: He said to him: The Holy One, Blessed be He, brought Abraham
and sat him at His right,
and we would throw dust and it became swords,
straw, and it became arrows,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers שם's question from step 40.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ה׳ seated אברהם at His right, and the dust and straw they threw miraculously became swords and arrows.

steps.title: Two verses support the miracle
steps.stepSummary: Two פסוקים are brought: one from תהלים about sitting at ה׳'s right, and one from ישעיהו about a sword like dust and a bow like straw.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'A psalm of David. ה׳ says to my master: Sit at My right, until I make your enemies your footstool.' And it is written: 'Who aroused one from the east, whom righteousness calls to its feet? He gives nations before him and makes him rule over kings; his sword makes them like dust, his bow like windblown straw.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings two פסוקים to back up each part of אליעזר's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in תהלים matches 'He sat אברהם at His right.' The פסוק in ישעיהו, about one 'from the east,' matches the dust and straw that became weapons: 'his sword like dust, his bow like straw.'

keyTerms.meaning: who aroused one from the east

phrases.english: as it is stated: "A Psalm of David.
The Lord says to my master: Sit to My right,
until I make your enemies your footstool,"
phrases.notes: תהלים 110:1

phrases.english: and it is written: "Who has raised up one from the east,
at whose steps victory attends?
He gives nations before him, and makes him rule over kings;
his sword makes them as the dust,
his bow as driven straw."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 41:2. Here the גמרא reads it as dust turning into a sword and straw turning into a bow.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings פסוקים to support אליעזר's answer.
steps.raayaObject: That ה׳ seated אברהם at His right and turned dust and straw into weapons.
steps.whatToRemember: The war of the kings was won by a miracle: ה׳ seated אברהם at His right, and dust and straw became swords and arrows.

steps.title: נחום איש גם זו's habit of saying 'גם זו לטובה'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces נחום איש גם זו, who said 'גם זו לטובה' about everything that happened to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: נחום איש גם זו had a habit: about anything that happened to him, he would say, 'This too is for the good.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new story. First it introduces נחום איש גם זו and his famous habit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This background is needed to understand the story that follows. His name 'גם זו' connects to his saying, 'גם זו לטובה.' The story is placed here because it is connected to the miracle of dust turning into weapons.

keyTerms.meaning: Nachum, the man of Gam Zo
this too is for the good

phrases.aramaic: נַחוּם אִישׁ גַּם זוֹ הֲוָה רְגִיל,
phrases.english: Nachum of Gam Zo was accustomed
that whatever happened to him,
he would say: "This too is for the good."

steps.triggerLanguage: נַחוּם אִישׁ גַּם זוֹ הֲוָה רְגִיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the שם and אליעזר conversations to a new related story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: נחום איש גם זו always said 'גם זו לטובה' about whatever happened to him.

steps.title: The Jewish people plan to send a gift to the emperor
steps.stepSummary: One day the Jewish people wanted to send a gift to the קיסר, and they began discussing who should bring it.
steps.simpleTranslation: One day the Jewish people wanted to send a gift to the קיסר. They said: With...
steps.whatsHappening: The story of נחום begins. This step sets the scene, and the sentence continues past this section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The setting is a gift for the Roman emperor. The words 'They said: With...' start a discussion about who should take the gift, which is finished in the next section.
steps.confusionAlert: The text stops in the middle of a sentence ('בהדי'). It is not a full thought yet; it continues next.

phrases.english: One day the Jewish people wanted
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets, ישראל, is added in the corrected wording.

phrases.english: to send a gift to the emperor.
They said: With

steps.triggerLanguage: יוֹמָא חַד בְּעוֹ יִשְׂרָאֵל לְשַׁדּוֹרֵי דּוֹרוֹן לְקֵיסָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the actual story about נחום, after the introduction of his habit.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The story begins with the Jewish people planning to send a gift to the emperor.
